metadata.title: Seed Domain: Everyday Physical World
metadata.description: Machine-parseable seed graph for everyday physical-world relation motifs. This is an external-world domain scaffold, not a full physics model.
notes: This graph is separate from the six-month child seed but uses the same relation grammar.
The first version emphasizes contrast pairs and counterfactual-friendly physical motifs.

layers.label: Physical Observation Channels
layers.description: Observable physical inputs such as contact, motion, sound, temperature, and material state.

layers.label: Physical Relational Invariants
layers.description: Reusable comparison, support, path, threshold, and state-change relations.

layers.label: Physical Properties
layers.description: Predictive summaries of material, surface, shape, flow, thermal, and force behavior.

layers.label: Everyday Object Handles
layers.description: Concrete handles used for physical-world contrast examples.

layers.label: Physical Event Outcomes
layers.description: Reusable event outcomes such as roll, slide, overflow, leak, cut, mark, and slip.

nodes.label: visual observation
nodes.summary: Source for shape, position, motion, light, shadow, containment, and visible state change.

nodes.label: sound observation
nodes.summary: Source for impact sound, vibration, loudness, resonance, and damping.

nodes.label: contact and pressure observation
nodes.summary: Source for contact, pressure, deformation, support, friction, and cutting.

nodes.label: temperature observation
nodes.summary: Source for heating, cooling, melting, boiling, conduction, and burning.

nodes.label: motion observation
nodes.summary: Source for falling, rolling, sliding, spinning, stopping, flowing, and rising.

nodes.label: material state observation
nodes.summary: Source for solid, liquid, gas, granular, porous, elastic, brittle, and plastic behavior.

nodes.label: same/different
nodes.summary: Compares whether objects, states, or outcomes match or differ.

nodes.label: before/after
nodes.summary: Orders physical states and events in time.

nodes.label: more/less
nodes.summary: Compares amount, force, load, speed, heat, sound, and resistance.

nodes.label: touching/not touching
nodes.summary: Tracks whether objects or materials are in contact.

nodes.label: moves/stops
nodes.summary: Tracks change in motion, rest, slowing, stopping, and starting.

nodes.label: supported/unsupported
nodes.summary: Tracks whether an object has sufficient support or becomes unstable.

nodes.label: support base
nodes.summary: Represents the area or geometry that supports an object or stack.

nodes.label: center of support
nodes.summary: Represents whether weight or mass is positioned within the support base.

nodes.label: inside/outside
nodes.summary: Tracks whether material or object content is within a boundary.

nodes.label: open/closed
nodes.summary: Tracks whether a path, container, circuit, or boundary permits transfer.

nodes.label: path blocked/unblocked
nodes.summary: Tracks whether flow, motion, or transfer is blocked by an obstacle.

nodes.label: state change
nodes.summary: Tracks transformation of material, shape, phase, mark, burn, break, or deformation.

nodes.label: threshold
nodes.summary: Represents enough force, heat, stretch, capacity, or sharpness to change outcome.

nodes.label: energy transfer
nodes.summary: Tracks transfer through impact, heat, vibration, elastic storage, electric circuit, or motion.

nodes.label: object fall and impact
nodes.summary: Unsupported object moves downward, impacts a surface, and produces outcome depending on material and surface.

nodes.label: material impact outcome
nodes.summary: Same impact frame produces different sound, bounce, deformation, or break outcomes based on material properties.

nodes.label: surface friction and motion
nodes.summary: Surface friction modifies rolling, sliding, resistance, traction, and stopping.

nodes.label: push-slide resistance
nodes.summary: Pushing an object causes more or less sliding depending on load and surface resistance.

nodes.label: slippery surface traction
nodes.summary: Wet or low-friction surface reduces traction and increases slipping risk.

nodes.label: object stack stability
nodes.summary: Stack height, width, support base, and nudge determine whether a stack stays stable or tips.

nodes.label: partial support tipping
nodes.summary: Object partly outside support can tip or fall when its weight relation crosses support boundary.

nodes.label: uneven support wobble
nodes.summary: Unequal support points create wobble, rocking, or instability.

nodes.label: pour-fill container
nodes.summary: Liquid moves through an opening into a container and changes fill level.

nodes.label: capacity and overflow
nodes.summary: If incoming liquid exceeds container capacity, liquid leaves the container.

nodes.label: constrained flow path
nodes.summary: Liquid or material follows a constrained path such as pipe, channel, or opening.

nodes.label: blocked flow
nodes.summary: A plug or blockage interrupts a flow path.

nodes.label: leak through opening
nodes.summary: Liquid leaves a container through an unintended opening.

nodes.label: absorption and porosity
nodes.summary: Porous or absorbent material takes in liquid and changes wetness or state.

nodes.label: squeeze release liquid
nodes.summary: Pressure on wet porous material releases stored liquid and deforms the material.

nodes.label: immiscible separation
nodes.summary: Two liquids contact but remain separated rather than uniformly mixed.

nodes.label: dissolution and mixing
nodes.summary: A soluble solid disperses into liquid and becomes less visible as separate particles.

nodes.label: heat transfer
nodes.summary: Heat moves between materials or regions with different temperatures.

nodes.label: phase change melting
nodes.summary: Solid material becomes liquid when heat transfer passes a phase-change threshold.

nodes.label: boiling vapor rise
nodes.summary: Heating liquid to boiling produces vapor that rises from the liquid.

nodes.label: thermal conduction by material
nodes.summary: Material type changes how quickly heat moves through an object.

nodes.label: combustion of flammable material
nodes.summary: Flame contact with flammable material can produce burning and irreversible state change.

nodes.label: edge-pressure cut
nodes.summary: Sharp edge plus pressure on a soft target can separate material.

nodes.label: blunt pressure deformation
nodes.summary: Blunt object plus pressure deforms a soft target without clean separation.

nodes.label: point pressure mark
nodes.summary: Pointed tip plus pressure on a marking surface creates a visible trace.

nodes.label: elastic stretch and return
nodes.summary: Elastic material changes shape under force and tends to return when force is removed.

nodes.label: elastic limit failure
nodes.summary: Too much stretch or force crosses a material threshold and causes break or permanent change.

nodes.label: spring compress and release
nodes.summary: Spring compression stores elastic energy and release produces motion.

nodes.label: plastic deformation retains shape
nodes.summary: Plastic material changes shape under force and retains much of the new shape.

nodes.label: wheel-axle rotation
nodes.summary: Wheel rotates around axle and supports rolling motion.

nodes.label: brake friction slows or stops
nodes.summary: Brake contact increases friction on a moving wheel and reduces motion.

nodes.label: load inertia and effort
nodes.summary: Heavier load requires greater effort to start or change motion.

nodes.label: lever-pivot balance
nodes.summary: Unequal weight around a pivot causes tilt or rotation.

nodes.label: air resistance during fall
nodes.summary: Air resistance modifies falling speed depending on mass, shape, and surface area.

nodes.label: magnet material selectivity
nodes.summary: Magnet attracts some materials and not others.

nodes.label: switch circuit activation
nodes.summary: Changing switch state can close a circuit and activate a device such as a light.

nodes.label: impact force and sound amplitude
nodes.summary: Stronger impact or vibration generally produces higher sound amplitude.

nodes.label: fragile
nodes.summary: Likely to break under impact or excess force.

nodes.label: brittle
nodes.summary: Breaks rather than bending substantially when stressed.

nodes.label: metallic resonance
nodes.summary: Metal impact often produces ringing or loud resonant sound.

nodes.label: plastic deformable
nodes.summary: Can deform without immediately shattering.

nodes.label: elastic
nodes.summary: Changes shape under force and tends to return when force is removed.

nodes.label: elastic limit
nodes.summary: Stretch or force limit beyond which material breaks or changes permanently.

nodes.label: hard
nodes.summary: Resists deformation and can produce stronger impact sound.

nodes.label: soft
nodes.summary: Deforms under pressure and often reduces impact force or sound.

nodes.label: round
nodes.summary: Curved shape that supports rolling under push or slope.

nodes.label: smooth surface
nodes.summary: Low texture variation, often lower sliding or rolling resistance.

nodes.label: rough surface
nodes.summary: High texture variation, often higher friction or resistance.

nodes.label: high friction
nodes.summary: Contact relation that resists sliding or rolling motion strongly.

nodes.label: low friction
nodes.summary: Contact relation that resists sliding or rolling motion weakly.

nodes.label: slippery wet surface
nodes.summary: Wet surface relation that can reduce traction for feet or wheels.

nodes.label: tall narrow
nodes.summary: Shape relation with higher tipping risk under side force.

nodes.label: wide stable
nodes.summary: Shape relation with broader support base and lower tipping risk.

nodes.label: container capacity
nodes.summary: Amount a container can hold before overflow.

nodes.label: opening
nodes.summary: Gap or path through which material can pass.

nodes.label: blockage
nodes.summary: Obstacle that prevents or reduces motion or flow along a path.

nodes.label: porous
nodes.summary: Has spaces that allow liquid or air to enter.

nodes.label: absorbent
nodes.summary: Takes in liquid rather than simply shedding it.

nodes.label: immiscible
nodes.summary: Does not mix uniformly with another liquid under ordinary conditions.

nodes.label: soluble
nodes.summary: Can dissolve into a liquid.

nodes.label: thermal conductor
nodes.summary: Transfers heat relatively quickly.

nodes.label: thermal insulator
nodes.summary: Transfers heat relatively slowly.

nodes.label: flammable
nodes.summary: Can burn when exposed to flame and sufficient conditions.

nodes.label: sharp edge
nodes.summary: Small edge contact area that concentrates pressure.

nodes.label: blunt edge
nodes.summary: Broad edge or surface that spreads pressure.

nodes.label: pointed tip
nodes.summary: Small tip contact area that concentrates pressure or leaves marks.

nodes.label: soft target
nodes.summary: Target material that deforms or separates under lower force.

nodes.label: heavy load
nodes.summary: Greater load that usually requires greater effort to move.

nodes.label: light load
nodes.summary: Smaller load that usually requires less effort to move.

nodes.label: pivot
nodes.summary: Point around which lever or seesaw rotation occurs.

nodes.label: magnetic material
nodes.summary: Material that is attracted by a magnet under ordinary conditions.

nodes.label: non-magnetic material
nodes.summary: Material that is not attracted by a magnet under ordinary conditions.

nodes.label: low sound amplitude
nodes.summary: Lower sound intensity from weaker vibration or impact.

nodes.label: high sound amplitude
nodes.summary: Higher sound intensity from stronger vibration or impact.

evaluation_questions.question: Why might a glass cup and a steel tumbler produce different outcomes when dropped from the same height?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: The fall-impact frame is the same, but material properties such as fragility, brittleness, and metallic resonance change the outcome.

evaluation_questions.question: Why does the same rubber ball roll differently on a smooth floor and a rough mat?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: Surface friction modifies rolling motion; smooth surfaces tend toward lower friction while rough surfaces tend toward higher friction.

evaluation_questions.question: Why is a tall narrow stack easier to tip than a wide stack when nudged?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: Stack stability depends on support base and center of support; tall-narrow and wide-stable shapes contrast in tipping risk.

evaluation_questions.question: What changes when water is poured into a full glass or into a bucket with a hole?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: A full container can overflow when capacity is exceeded, while a hole creates a leak path through an opening.

evaluation_questions.question: Why are cloth in water, salt in water, and oil in water different?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: Cloth absorbs through porosity, salt dissolves, and oil remains separated because it is immiscible with water.

evaluation_questions.question: Why does a metal spoon in hot tea behave differently from a wooden spoon?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: Both receive heat, but metal is treated as a stronger thermal conductor while wood is treated as a stronger thermal insulator.

evaluation_questions.question: What relation links melting ice, boiling water, and paper burning?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: All involve state change driven by heat transfer and thresholds, but burning also depends on flammable material.

evaluation_questions.question: Why does a knife cut tomato more easily than a spoon or blunt knife?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: A sharp edge concentrates pressure on a soft target and can cause cut separation; blunt pressure tends to deform instead.

evaluation_questions.question: Why do a rubber band, a spring, and clay differ after force is applied?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: Elastic objects tend to return or release stored energy, too much stretch can exceed a limit, and plastic material can retain the new shape.

evaluation_questions.question: Why is a loaded cart harder to push than an empty cart?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: The load relation changes inertia and effort; heavy load contrasts with light load.

evaluation_questions.question: Why does a feather fall differently from a stone in still air?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: Air resistance modifies the fall relation differently depending on object properties such as mass, shape, and surface area.

evaluation_questions.question: Why does a magnet pull iron pins but not a wooden pencil?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: Magnetic attraction is material selective; iron has the magnetic-material relation while wood is treated as non-magnetic.

evaluation_questions.question: What relation is active when a switch is turned on and the light comes on?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: The switch changes an open/closed circuit relation and can cause the light-on event if the device and circuit work.

evaluation_questions.question: Why is walking on wet floor tiles riskier than dry floor tiles?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: Wet slippery surface supports low friction, reducing traction and increasing slip risk.
